description: Mapping verified agroecological zones with NASA data to protect clean farmland.
summary: Terra Limpia moves from estimating pesticide risk to verifying clean land. This decision-support tool helps farmers choose resilient crop rotations by adding the agrochemical legacy of each zone. It combines NASA's PEST-CHEMGRIDS pesticide estimates (2015–2025) with NASA POWER climate data, SMAP soil moisture and Landsat/MODIS vegetation history, and calibrates them with ground truth: Córdoba's digital spray prescriptions, farmer records and random lab tests. Each zone is classified as clean, in transition or high exposure, and receives rotations that fit its climate, soil and history. It is urgent: 64% of the world's farmland is at risk of pesticide pollution, and the world has four harvests left to halve that risk by 2030. We propose that zones verified clean for three or more years automatically become candidates for FAO's Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS), keeping that land with the farmers who work it without agrochemicals. The pilot starts in Córdoba, Argentina; the method works anywhere with open NASA data.
details:
What it does: Terra Limpia classifies farmland into clean, in-transition and high-exposure zones by combining NASA pesticide estimates with climate, soil moisture and vegetation history, calibrated with ground truth (digital spray prescriptions, farmer records, random lab tests). It then suggests crop rotations that fit each zone's climate, soil and agrochemical history.

Benefits: rotations fit to the land's real history; agroecological farmers can prove clean practices; governments get evidence to protect clean land.

Impact: supports Kunming-Montreal Target 7 (halve pesticide risk by 2030) and proposes that zones verified clean for 3+ years automatically become candidates for FAO's GIAHS programme, keeping that land with farmers who work without agrochemicals.

Tools: NASA PEST-CHEMGRIDS, NASA POWER, SMAP, Landsat/MODIS via AppEEARS; slides and a map mockup.

Creativity: turns invisible farming practices into a readable map and links soil data to global heritage protection.

Factors considered: coarse ~10 km model data, lab costs, farmer privacy (zones, never owners), land speculation, legal liability, national sovereignty.

Authorship: the original concept (agroecological traceability, clean-farmland mapping, heritage protection, automatic GIAHS candidacy) was created by the team owner. An AI assistant (Claude) helped with research, structuring, drafting, translation and slide design.

Academic advisor: Prof. Veronica Mailen Celiz, IGTP de la UPC.
